description:
Functional specifications covered with associated files to edit/add: existing lib/zaq/engine/connect/oauth.ex and oauth_state.ex, new OAuth authorization attempt schema/context and migration, PersonCredentials start/reconnect functions, current callback boundary only for secure backend integration, tests under test/zaq/engine/connect/ and existing OAuth controller tests if touched. Reuse existing provider exchange/authorize infrastructure; no Person UI. Start accepts eligible credential and trusted Person context, never browser ownership attrs. Persist short-lived opaque attempt with credential/person/provider/config revision, fixed redirect URI and encrypted PKCE verifier; browser state contains opaque unguessable identity signed using existing state protection. No verifier or secret attrs in signed-but-readable state. Callback verifies state expiry/signature, provider equals current credential, trusted initiating identity still valid, policy eligible, configuration unchanged and attempt unused. Bind grant ownership from server-side attempt, ignoring browser person_id/credential_id substitutions. Preserve existing org/user callback flows deliberately; new Person path must not be bypassable via old build_authorize_url context owner fields. Reconnect replaces current canonical grant deterministically, emits mutation event, preserves previous valid grant on failed exchange. Callback response returns sanitized status/error only; no raw provider body or inspected secrets. Fix any touched callback message channel redaction/origin behavior needed to avoid exposing tokens, without UI redesign.

Tests to add before implementation: start missing/forged identity, signature tampering, expired/replayed/concurrent callback, credential/provider/redirect substitution, deleted or merged initiator, policy disabled during flow, config changed during flow, wrong owner attrs, encrypted verifier/token/refresh_token, reconnect uniqueness and failed exchange retention, attempt cleanup. Verify attacker cannot start person flow through legacy generic OAuth entry point.

Branches/paths validated: claim attempt atomically before external exchange; no database transaction held during network IO; ambiguous/exchange failure consumes attempt and requires fresh start rather than replay; successful exchange finalization rechecks revision/person/policy in transaction. Define and test cancellation/retention TTL; no authorization code persisted or logged. Existing provider-specific administrative OAuth configuration stays immutable to People.

Mocking plan: mock only external authorize/exchange HTTP; real state signature, Repo, authorization, transactions and event jobs. Use controlled time/randomness via production seams; no global env patching. Documentations to update: OAuth moduledocs/types, docs/services/engine.md flow and replay contract, docs/services/system-config.md encrypted attempt fields. >=95% touched-file coverage.

2026-09-14 FINAL USER-APPROVED STORAGE DECISION: canonical grants reuse owner_type/owner_id (org with NULL ID or person with non-null ID) and resource_type=connect_credential/resource_id=credential_id string. Native type/shape and explicit non-null/equality CHECKs plus existing credential_id FK; partial unique org/person slots across statuses. No binding_type, duplicate person_id, extra Person FK, triggers or guard rows. Server derives resource pair and configuration auth fields; secret_binding stays independent. Trusted canonical storage checks literal current active Person, without authenticating callers or resolving aliases. Concurrent orphan grants/secrets are an accepted residual risk. IDs must not be reused operationally; no silent reidentification through stale aliases; synchronous erasure is not guaranteed. Later resolver must check Person exists/eligible BEFORE policy selection even disabled, and missing/stale Person errors NEVER fall back globally. Authenticated writes and OAuth/refresh must recheck current identity; lifecycle cleanup/reconciliation and later distributed server invalidation remain unimplemented in storage task .1.
